A.explanation: The occupied division operates the parent state's hostile framework (extremist designation, transition ban, no recognition) through wartime occupation authorities with no rule of law. Documented practices exceed statute: occupying forces specifically searched for LGBTIQ+ people (81 known victims of detention/violence), a gay man was shot and buried behind a checkpoint, and a notorious informal detention site was used for intimidation, ransom and forced labour. Trans people are specifically trapped by document mismatch at checkpoints. No monitor, remedy or protective institution operates. This is state-directed organised targeting with lethal outcomes and zero recourse - the worst tier of the precedence ladder, near the bottom of the scale. Only the absence of a documented judicial execution pathway keeps it marginally above 0.05.

entry_documents.exposure: Appearance-document mismatch prevents trans people from leaving through checkpoints; occupying military specifically search for LGBTIQ+ people.
entry_documents.interaction: Checkpoint discovery routes directly to detention/violence by occupying forces.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Notorious informal detention site used for intimidation, ransom and forced labour; acute risk of sexual violence in detention per UN reporting; a gay man shot and buried behind a checkpoint.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Discovery by military or occupation administration leads to insults, violence, extortion, restriction of freedom and threats to life.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Occupying authorities apply parent-state propaganda law, transition ban and extremist designation; wartime arbitrariness governs all facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No functioning institution distinguishes visitor from resident.

care_services.exposure: Parent-state 2023 transition ban and healthcare prohibition apply; discrimination blocks services.
care_services.interaction: Medication discovery at checkpoints is an outing and seizure risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: LGBT identity itself treated as target: occupying forces hunt LGBTIQ+ people; 'perverted unions' persecution lineage; extortion and threats to life documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Occupation administration is both prosecutor and armed actor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent framework criminalises 'desire to change sex' propaganda touching minors; no minor-specific occupation finding, but wartime targeting is indiscriminate.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian outed at checkpoint endangers the child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Lethal violence by occupation forces documented (checkpoint killing); no police response exists - occupiers are the threat.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims cannot report to any authority.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No monitor, remedy or protective institution operates; almost all openly LGBT residents have fled.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Flight is the only mitigation, and document mismatch blocks even leaving.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Consular or external help has no documented channel.

anchor_checks.comparison: A matches 0.05-C's structure: armed authority hunts people by identity, lethal detention harm is documented, no appeal body functions. A lacks a publicly announced execution verdict, placing it barely above 0.05.
A is materially worse than 0.15-C: morality-unit sweeps there end in prosecution and bail games; in A the actors are armed occupiers who kill and detain for ransom with zero judicial facade at all.
Vastly worse than 0.25-C (birth-sex custody with some court recognition of safety rights). A has no courts, documented checkpoint killings, and organised hunting of LGBTIQ+ people.

A.synthesis: Every journey stage in A runs through armed occupation authority with no independent institution. Discovery - via checkpoint documents, raids, or denunciation - leads along a documented path to extortion, forced labour, sexual violence and killing, with 81 known victims and a recorded checkpoint execution. The parent framework's extremist designation supplies legal cover; wartime lawlessness removes even the theoretical remedy layer that ordinary hostile states retain. Flight is blocked by the same document mismatch that creates exposure. This is the tier-1/tier-2 combination at maximum severity with zero recourse; only the lack of a documented judicial execution pathway separates it from the absolute floor.

B.explanation: B sits under the full parent-state regime: extremist designation of the LGBT movement (participation 2-6 years, organising 6-10 years), all-audiences propaganda law (fines, 15-day detention, repeat criminal exposure up to 4 years; publishing staff facing 12 years), 101 convictions, raids on venues, a custody death, no recognition, no anti-discrimination law, hostile society (74% rejection). Enforcement is active, current and escalating. A visitor outed faces the same machinery; document mismatch is a universal exposure at any ID check. Unlike dossier A's occupied division, B has ordinary courts and no documented lethal targeting of visitors or organised hunts - enforcement centres on expression, association and symbols rather than mere presence. That places it just above the 0.15 band anchors but clearly below any 0.25 anchor, since imprisonment after discovery is a realistic outcome and one detainee died in custody.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport remains as issued; no marker change possible; mismatch at any check forces outing. Extremist-designation screening could treat LGBT affiliation adversely.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at hotel or police check feeds the propaganda/extremism enforcement chain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Extremism charges carry 2-6 years (participation) and 6-10 (organising); 15-day administrative detention; one pretrial detainee died; venue raids with patrons photographed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under designation leads to pretrial custody with documented lethal risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custody placement for trans people not specifically documented but parent regime denies all recognition; masked raids on venues show facility-level enforcement.

care_services.exposure: 2023 transition ban and healthcare prohibition apply nationwide; possession/import of medication not documented as enforced against visitors.
care_services.interaction: Medication discovery risks outing under a state that treats transition as banned.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State frames the LGBT movement as extremist; display of rainbow colours prosecuted; publishing staff face 12 years for LGBT-themed fiction; 139 people affected Dec 2022-Mar 2024; 98 administrative convictions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Any visible association or expression triggers escalating charges.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law specifically prohibits material giving minors 'desire to change sex'; a trans guardian with a minor faces heightened scrutiny under child-protection framing.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's outing risks state inquiry into fitness as parent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Venue raids, arrests and public hostility documented; hate crimes not recorded and not an aggravating factor; 74% societal rejection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are enforcement actors, not protectors; reporting increases exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; no recourse for bias violence; refugee-designation assessments confirm persecution-level treatment; courts enforce the hostile statutes efficiently.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule of law operates against, not for, the outed traveller.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest match: immigration/morality detention with real prison exposure, lethal custody risk, courts deferring to the state, embassy access limited. B's statutes carry explicit multi-year terms and an active conviction count, though B documents fewer custody-abuse specifics.

B is worse than 0.25-D: that anchor's morality enforcement yields fines and short terms with appellate annulment; B's extremist-designation charges run to 6-10 years with three criminal convictions and a custodial death, and 0.25-D shows some judicial pushback B does not.

Materially worse than 0.35-A, whose sanction is exclusion and humiliation; B's documented outcomes include multi-year imprisonment, custodial death and 12-year charges, so B must sit well below this anchor.

B.synthesis: B's combined regime is the parent state applied uniformly: an enforced, escalating criminalisation of LGBT identity itself via the extremism designation, plus propaganda statutes reaching expression and even literature. For an outed visitor the operative pathway runs document mismatch or observed association -> police stop or raid -> administrative or criminal charge -> pretrial custody where a death has occurred. Rule of law functions only as an instrument of the hostile policy. A discreet, non-expressing visitor may pass unnoticed, but discovery at any ID check carries realistic multi-year imprisonment risk, no anti-discrimination recourse, no recorded hate-crime handling, and 74% societal hostility behind it. Calibration: above the occupied-division jurisdiction (no organised lethal hunts, ordinary courts exist) but below every 0.25-band anchor because imprisonment, not fines, is the documented design of the regime.
